latest_news.title: Nedbank Eswatini Limited Declares E193 Million Dividend for FY2024 Ahead of 50th AGM
latest_news.content:
Nedbank Eswatini Limited has announced a final dividend of 787 cents per share, amounting to a total payout of E193 million for the financial year ended 31 December 2024.

The dividend will be paid to shareholders registered in the company’s books by the close of business on 9 May 2025. The transfer books and register of members will be closed from 10 May to 16 May 2025, both days inclusive, to facilitate the dividend distribution. Payment is expected on or around 31 May 2025.
The company emphasized that all relevant liquidity, solvency, and capital requirements were met before declaring the dividend. Taxes will be withheld in accordance with local regulations for both resident and non-resident shareholders.

This declaration reflects Nedbank Eswatini’s continued strong financial performance and its commitment to delivering value to shareholders.

latest_news.title: Nedbank Eswatini Limited Announces 50th Annual General Meeting
latest_news.content:
Nedbank Eswatini Limited has officially announced that its 50th Annual General Meeting (AGM) will be held on 28 May 2025 at 14:00 at the Hilton Garden Inn, Mbabane. The notice, issued by Company Secretary M.A. Shongwe, outlines key agenda items for shareholders.
During the AGM, shareholders will:
•	Approve the minutes of the previous AGM held on 31 May 2024.
•	Receive and adopt the annual financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024, along with directors’ and auditors’ reports.
•	Appoint independent auditors for the upcoming year and approve their remuneration.
•	Confirm the remuneration paid to directors for 2024.
•	Acknowledge the transfer of SZL20.2 million to the Statutory Reserve Account, complying with the Financial Institutions Act, 2005.
•	Confirm the final dividend of 787 cents per share, totaling E193 million, payable to shareholders registered by 9 May 2025.
•	Re-elect retiring directors Mrs. S. Nkumane and Mr. G. Payne.
•	Confirm the appointment of new independent non-executive director Mrs. A. Brown and note the retirement of Mr. M. Maziya.
The meeting signifies a critical opportunity for shareholders to exercise their governance rights and affirm the company’s continued commitment to transparency and accountability.

latest_news.title: SWAPROP Issues Cautionary Statement on Interim Results Delay
latest_news.content:
Swaziland Property Investment Limited (SWAPROP), a property investment holding company listed on the Eswatini Stock Exchange (ESE), has issued a cautionary announcement regarding the delay in releasing its interim financial results for the six months ended 31 December 2024. The company advises shareholders to exercise caution when dealing in its linked units and to consult their financial advisors as necessary, pending further announcements. 
While the specific reasons for the delay were not disclosed, SWAPROP has assured stakeholders that the forthcoming financial statements will not differ materially from previous disclosures. This assurance aims to maintain investor confidence during the interim period.
The company anticipates releasing the delayed interim results by the end of June 2025. Shareholders and investors are encouraged to stay informed through official channels for updates on the publication date.
SWAPROP remains committed to transparency and upholding the principles of accountability and integrity as outlined in the King Reports’ guidelines on Corporate Governance. The company continues to focus on enhancing shareholder value through strategic property investments and effective management of its property portfolio

latest_news.title: Nkonyeni Precast Limited Interim Financial Statements 31 December 2024
latest_news.content:
Nkonyeni Pre-Cast Limited Reports Profit and Strategic Growth in Interim Results
Nkonyeni Pre-Cast Limited (NPC), a listed entity on the Eswatini Stock Exchange, has released its Reviewed Interim Financial Results for the six months ended 31 December 2024, showcasing operational resilience and strategic progress despite economic headwinds.
NPC recorded a profit of E238,750 for the period, up from E50,437 in the prior comparable period. Revenue reached E25.7 million, while cost of sales stood at E13.4 million, resulting in a gross profit of over E12.3 million. The improvement reflects strong cost management and strategic business initiatives.
A key milestone was securing E24 million in funding from a local bank, earmarked for the acquisition of a raw material source, asset financing, and working capital. The company also successfully launched the NPC102 bond program, closing in January 2025.
Highlights from the period include:
•	Launch of bagged aggregates, boosting sales in the DIY and small contractor segment by 5%.
•	Introduction of a 15-year warranty on Swazi Tiles concrete roof tiles.
•	Awards for Product of the Year (Large Enterprise – NPC, SME – Swazi Tile) at the Eswatini Quality Awards 2024.
Looking ahead, NPC is still pursuing equity interest expansion and a capital raising initiative, aiming to enhance shareholder value and broaden its market footprint. The company reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, innovation, and corporate governance as part of its long-term growth strategy.
These results reflect NPC’s robust performance and its pivotal role in Eswatini’s construction and manufacturing sectors.

latest_news.title: Nkonyeni Pre-Cast Limited makes first coupon on Bond programme
latest_news.content: Nkonyeni Pre-Cast Limited is pleased to announce that it has paid a coupon to bondholders due on 30rd September 2024 under its NPC100 Medium-Term Note Bond Programme. The 10- year Programme was Auctioned on the 05th of April 2024 at a variable interest rate of prime plus 1.5% per annum maturing 05 April 2034. The next coupon payment is due on 30th March 2025. The bonds are listed and admitted to trading on the Eswatini Stock Exchange.

companies.name: Eswatini First National Bank
companies.about: First National Bank can trace its origins back to the Eastern Province Bank, which was formed in Grahamstown, South Africa in 1838. By 1874, the bank had four branches - Grahamstown, Middelburg, Cradock and Queenstown. Due to a recession, the bank was bought out in 1874 by the Oriental Bank Corporation (OBC). However, as a result of financial difficulties being experienced in India, the OBC decided to withdraw from South Africa. The Bank of Africa was subsequently formed in 1879 to take over OBC's business in South Africa.
